title: Bounded mission work
verification: Source guidance only; runtime speedup remains unproven. Cleanup teaching is project-agnostic: the walker removes everything the walk creates (repositories, accounts, records the product registered) with the product's own commands, creates GitHub fixture repositories as private, records each exact OWNER/NAME when created (including one the product creates) and deletes it with gh repo delete OWNER/NAME --yes, never hands cleanup to steering, and reports every refusal, recovery and remaining resource for the final verdict. For host missions, walk-end only removes staging and restores the host. Hostless missions use controller tools, record a docket without a lease, and owe no host reset, restore or reset debt. Yoke-specific Machine, project and repository cleanup lives in docs/testing-verification/qa-fixture-cleanup.md; installed proof remains unverified. Host mission artifact teaching copies target bytes with yoke qa mission host-copy --from TARGET_PATH --to LOCAL_PATH into the walker's local scratch directory and uploads with --content-file; host-copy streams the bytes through each host adapter's SSH connection, bounds them at the 20 MB QA artifact limit, and refuses missing files and any path that resolves inside the mission scratch directory, which remains secret staging. Source tests run each adapter's real reader script locally and prove byte-equal non-UTF-8 payloads and every named refusal; a source-build mission walk on the Linux Test Machine copied 300000 random bytes with matching sha256 and saw both scratch and missing-path refusals. Real-host copies through the macOS and Windows adapters remain unverified. Missions needing a test message send it from the Test Machine's own Yoke identity through yoke qa mission host-command; the walker never sends controller Fleet mail. This is source teaching, not new delivery proof.
